question: Which vehicles fall into CDL Class A?
choice_a: Any combination of vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 or more pounds, provided the towed unit's GVWR exceeds 10,000 pounds
choice_b: Any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 or more pounds
choice_c: Any single vehicle with a GVWR less than 26,001 pounds
choice_d: Any vehicle designed to carry fewer than 16 passengers
explanation: Class A Combination Vehicles are any combination with a GCWR of 26,001 or more pounds, provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed is more than 10,000 pounds.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Classifications

question: A Class B CDL covers which type of vehicle?
choice_a: A combination vehicle with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more
choice_b: Any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 or more pounds, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle not in excess of 10,000 pounds GVWR
choice_c: Only vehicles that haul hazardous materials
choice_d: Any vehicle towing a trailer over 10,000 pounds GVWR
explanation: Class B Heavy Straight Vehicles are any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 or more pounds, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle not exceeding 10,000 pounds GVWR.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Classifications

question: A single vehicle with a GVWR less than 26,001 pounds still requires a Class C CDL if it is:
choice_a: Used only for personal, non-commercial travel
choice_c: Designed to carry 16 or more passengers (including the driver), or used to transport placarded hazardous materials or select agents/toxins
explanation: Class C vehicles under 26,001 pounds GVWR are included in the CDL program only if designed to carry 16+ passengers including the driver, or used to transport hazardous materials requiring placarding (or select agents/toxins).
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Classifications

question: A CDL is required to drive a vehicle designed to transport how many passengers, including the driver?
explanation: You must have a CDL to operate a vehicle designed to transport 16 or more passengers, including the driver.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, 'You must have a CDL to operate'

question: A CDL is required for any single vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of:
explanation: You must have a CDL to operate any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, 'You must have a CDL to operate'

question: For a combination vehicle to require a CDL under the GCWR rule, the towed vehicle's GVWR must exceed:
explanation: A combination vehicle with a GCWR of 26,001 or more pounds requires a CDL provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed is in excess of 10,000 pounds.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, 'You must have a CDL to operate'

question: A driver who wants to haul any material requiring hazardous materials placarding must obtain which endorsement, which also requires an Entry Level Driver Training and TSA background check?
explanation: The Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement requires completing Entry Level Driver Training, passing a special written exam, and a TSA background check.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: Which endorsement must a Class A driver add before pulling double or triple trailers?
explanation: The Double and Triple Trailers (T) endorsement is required, and applicants must pass a special knowledge exam on the problems of pulling multiple trailers.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: The Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement is required for a tank with an individual rated capacity of more than how many gallons?
explanation: The N endorsement applies to tanks with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: The Passenger (P) endorsement is required for vehicles with a design capacity of how many people, including the driver?
explanation: Drivers who wish to drive a vehicle with a design capacity of 16 or more people, including the driver, must add a Passenger (P) endorsement.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: A driver who hauls hazardous materials or waste in a tank vehicle requiring placards must obtain which endorsement?
explanation: The Combination Hazardous Materials and Tank Vehicle (X) endorsement shows the driver has passed both the tank vehicle and hazardous materials knowledge exams.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: Which endorsement requires passing a special knowledge exam on safety considerations when transporting passengers in a bus used for student transport, plus skills tests in that vehicle?
explanation: The School Bus (S) endorsement requires a special knowledge exam, Entry Level Driver Training, and skills tests in a school bus.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: Which three endorsements may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)?
choice_a: Passenger (P), School bus (S), and Tank vehicle (N)
choice_b: Hazardous materials (H), Tank vehicle (N), and Double/Triple (T)
choice_d: School bus (S), Double/Triple (T), and Tank vehicle (N)
explanation: The manual specifies the only endorsements that may be added to a CLP are Passenger (P), School bus (S), and Tank vehicle (N).
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: If a CLP is issued with a Passenger (P) or School Bus (S) endorsement, what restriction must also be on it?
choice_a: An X restriction (no cargo in tank vehicle)
choice_b: A P restriction (no passengers in a CMV bus)
explanation: A CLP issued with a P or S endorsement must also contain a P restriction, meaning no passengers in a CMV bus.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: If a CLP is issued with a Tanker (N) endorsement, what restriction must also be on it?
choice_c: An X restriction (no cargo in a CMV tank vehicle)
explanation: A CLP issued with an N (Tanker) endorsement must also contain an X restriction, meaning no cargo in a CMV tank vehicle.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: How many questions are on the Utah hazardous materials (H) endorsement written knowledge test?
explanation: According to the Utah Driver License Division, the hazardous materials (H) endorsement written knowledge test consists of 30 questions.
source_note: dld.utah.gov/cdl-info/

question: How many questions are on the Utah tank vehicle (N) endorsement written knowledge test?
explanation: According to the Utah Driver License Division, the tank vehicle (N) endorsement written knowledge test consists of 20 questions.
source_note: dld.utah.gov/cdl-info/

question: What does restriction code 'E' mean on a CDL?
choice_a: No cargo in a CMV tank vehicle
explanation: The 'E' restriction means the driver is restricted from operating a CMV equipped with a manual transmission, because the skills test was taken in an automatic-transmission vehicle.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: A driver with a 'K' restriction on their CDL is limited to:
explanation: The 'K' restriction indicates the driver has certified as Non-Excepted or Excepted Intrastate and is restricted from operating a CMV in interstate commerce.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: An 'L' restriction on a CDL means the driver is restricted from operating:
choice_a: A vehicle with a manual transmission
choice_b: A tractor-trailer connected by a fifth wheel
choice_d: A CMV equipped with any type of air brakes
explanation: The 'L' restriction (No Air brake equipped CMV) applies when an applicant fails or does not take the air brake knowledge test, or takes the skills test in a vehicle without air brakes.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: An 'O' restriction on a CDL means the driver is restricted from operating:
choice_a: A tractor-trailer combination requiring a Group A CDL connected by a fifth wheel
choice_c: A vehicle with a manual transmission
explanation: The 'O' restriction (No tractor trailer CMV) applies when the skills test for a Group A CDL is taken in a combination vehicle connected by a pintle hook or other non-fifth-wheel connection.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: A 'V' restriction on a CDL indicates:
choice_a: The driver is restricted to intrastate operation
choice_b: The driver has been issued a medical variance by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration
choice_c: The driver may only operate an empty tank vehicle
choice_d: The driver must wear corrective lenses
explanation: The 'V' restriction shows there is information about a medical variance on the driver's CDLIS record, as required when the state is notified of a variance under 49 CFR 383.73(o)(3).
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: An 'X' restriction on a CLP or CDL means the holder:
choice_a: May not drive during nighttime hours
choice_b: May not operate a vehicle with a manual transmission
choice_c: May only operate an empty tank vehicle, and may not operate a tank vehicle that previously held hazmat and has not been purged
explanation: A CLP holder with an N endorsement and X restriction may only operate an empty tank vehicle, and is prohibited from operating any tank vehicle that previously contained hazardous materials that has not been purged of residue.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: A 'Z' restriction on a CDL restricts the driver from operating a CMV equipped with:
choice_d: Any braking system operating fully on the air brake principle (i.e., other than air-over-hydraulic brakes)
explanation: The 'Z' restriction (No full air brake equipped CMV) applies when the skills test is taken in a vehicle with air-over-hydraulic brakes, restricting the driver from CMVs with full air brakes.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: To remove an 'E', 'L', or 'O' restriction from a Utah CDL, a driver must:
choice_a: Obtain a qualifying permit and pass the applicable skills test(s)
choice_c: Wait one year with a clean driving record
choice_d: Pass only the general knowledge test again
explanation: The manual states that to remove a CDL 'E', 'L', or 'O' restriction, a driver must obtain a qualifying permit and pass the skills test(s); modified skills tests are not permitted in Utah.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: Utah law requires CDL applicants to provide their driver license and a current Medical Examiner's Certificate, along with a minimum of how much experience as a licensed driver?
explanation: Utah law requires all CDL applicants to provide their driver license, a minimum of one year experience as a licensed driver, and the most current Medical Examiner's Certificate.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.1.3 - Utah CDL Requirements

question: When a Utah applicant receives their Commercial Driver Instruction Permit (CDIP) and surrenders their driver license, what does the CDIP allow them to do?
choice_a: Drive any commercial motor vehicle unsupervised
choice_d: Drive a school bus with passengers
explanation: After surrendering their driver license upon receiving the Utah CDIP, the CDIP allows the applicant to continue operating their regular motor vehicle.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.1.3 - Utah CDL Requirements

question: Under Utah rules, CDL applicants under the age of 21 are restricted from obtaining which endorsements?
explanation: The manual notes that CDL applicants under age 21 are restricted from obtaining the Passenger, School Bus, or Hazmat endorsements.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.1.3 - Utah CDL Requirements

question: How long is a Utah Commercial Driver Instruction Permit (CDIP/CLP) valid?
explanation: According to the Utah Driver License Division, a CDL learner permit (CDIP) is valid for 180 days.
source_note: dld.utah.gov/cdl-info/

question: Before taking the CDL skills test in Utah, a CLP holder must have held the permit for at least how many days?
explanation: Per the Utah Driver License Division, a CLP must be held for at least 14 days before the applicant may take the skills test.
source_note: dld.utah.gov/cdl-driving-test/

question: On a Utah CDL, restriction code 'A' means:
explanation: Under Utah's state restriction codes, 'A' indicates no restrictions on the license.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.4 - State of Utah Restrictions

question: On a Utah CDL, restriction code 'B' requires the driver to:
choice_a: Use a prosthetic aid while driving
choice_c: Drive only vehicles with outside rearview mirrors
explanation: Utah restriction code 'B' requires the driver to wear corrective lenses while driving.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.4 - State of Utah Restrictions

question: Utah restriction code 'U' restricts a motorcyclist to:
explanation: Utah restriction code 'U' restricts a motorcyclist to riding only three-wheeled motorcycles.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.4 - State of Utah Restrictions

question: Utah restriction code 'R' applies to which driver?
choice_a: A driver restricted to intrastate operation
choice_b: A CLP holder with an H endorsement, prohibiting them from operating a CMV of the class/type applied for that is also equipped with hazardous materials
choice_c: A driver restricted to vehicles with automatic transmission
choice_d: A driver who must have an ignition interlock device
explanation: Utah restriction code 'R' applies to a CDL driver with an H endorsement who obtained a CLP, prohibiting them from operating a CMV of the license class/type applied for that is also equipped with hazardous materials.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.4 - State of Utah Restrictions

question: Utah restriction code '1' requires the driver to:
choice_a: Drive only vehicles with automatic transmission
choice_b: Drive only on roads posted 40 mph or less
choice_c: Have an ignition interlock device installed in the vehicle they are operating
choice_d: Use a mechanical aid or compensatory device
explanation: Utah restriction code '1' requires the driver to have an ignition interlock device installed in the motor vehicle they are operating.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.4 - State of Utah Restrictions

question: Utah restriction code '7' requires that vehicles the driver operates be equipped with:
explanation: Utah restriction code '7' requires that vehicles the driver operates be equipped with an automatic transmission.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.4 - State of Utah Restrictions

question: On a Utah CDL, which endorsement code represents 'Taxi'?
explanation: Among Utah's state endorsement codes, 'Z' represents Taxi.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.5 - State of Utah Endorsements

question: To maintain a Utah H (Hazardous Materials) endorsement, a driver must pass a TSA background check how often?
explanation: To maintain the H endorsement, Utah applicants must pass a TSA background check every 5 years, plus a written exam upon original issuance or renewal.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.5 - State of Utah Endorsements

question: To maintain a Utah S (School Bus) endorsement, what must the driver do upon renewal of their Utah Driver License?
choice_a: Submit a new TSA background check
choice_d: Provide a new Medical Examiner's Certificate only
explanation: To maintain the S endorsement, applicants are required to pass a written exam upon renewal of the Utah Driver License.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.5 - State of Utah Endorsements

question: Which of these describes driving in 'interstate commerce'?
choice_a: Driving a CMV entirely within one state with no out-of-state cargo or passengers
choice_b: Driving only for a private, non-business purpose
choice_c: Driving only vehicles under 26,001 pounds GVWR
choice_d: Driving from one state to another, or within a state as part of a trip that crosses state lines or involves cargo/passengers moving to or from another state
explanation: Interstate commerce includes driving from one state to another or a foreign country, or a trip within a state where the vehicle crosses state lines or the cargo/passengers are part of a trip beginning or ending in another state.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.1 - Interstate or Intrastate Commerce

question: Which self-certification category do most CDL holders who drive CMVs in interstate commerce fall under?
explanation: The manual states that most CDL holders who drive CMVs in interstate commerce are non-excepted interstate commerce drivers, requiring a medical examiner's certificate.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.2 - Inter/Intrastate Commerce: Status

question: Which of the following is listed as an example of 'excepted' interstate commerce activity that does not require a federal medical examiner's certificate?
choice_a: Long-haul freight trucking between states for a for-hire carrier
choice_b: Transporting school children and/or school staff between home and school
choice_c: Hauling placarded hazardous materials across state lines
choice_d: Driving a for-hire interstate passenger bus route
explanation: Transporting school children and/or school staff between home and school is listed among the excepted interstate commerce activities that do not require a federal MEC.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.2 - Inter/Intrastate Commerce: Status

question: In Utah, a driver operates in 'Excepted Intrastate' commerce if they are:
choice_b: A farmer transporting agricultural products only
choice_c: Under 21 years of age and authorized to drive a CMV only in intrastate commerce
choice_d: Hauling hazardous materials within Utah only
explanation: In Utah, a driver operates in Excepted Intrastate commerce if they are under 21 years of age and authorized to drive a CMV only in intrastate commerce, and must have a K restriction added to the license.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.2 - Inter/Intrastate Commerce: Status

question: Where can a CDL applicant find a list of registered physicians authorized to perform the DOT medical exam?
choice_b: Through their employer's HR department only
choice_d: On the National Registry, found at www.fmcsa.dot.gov
explanation: The manual directs applicants to contact a registered physician from the National Registry, found at www.fmcsa.dot.gov.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.6 - Medical Examination

question: If a driver does not qualify for a Medical Examiner's Certificate (MEC), they may be eligible for what?
choice_a: A Utah 'K' restriction, allowing intrastate driving within Utah only
choice_b: An automatic exemption from all medical requirements
choice_d: A waiver good for interstate driving nationwide
explanation: If a driver does not qualify for an MEC, they may be eligible for a Utah 'K' restriction, allowing them to drive a CMV within the state of Utah only.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.6 - Medical Examination

question: How long is a Medical Examiner's Certificate (MEC) generally valid?
explanation: A Medical Examiner's Certificate is generally valid for 24 months from the date of examination.
source_note: dld.utah.gov/cdl-info/

question: A standard Utah MVR shows moving violations for how many previous years?
explanation: An MVR obtained at a Driver License office will show all moving violations for the previous three (3) years.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.7 - MVR

question: How long do drug and alcohol offenses stay on a Utah driver's MVR?
explanation: Drug and alcohol offenses stay on a driver's MVR for 10 years, compared to 3 years for standard moving violations.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.7 - MVR

question: Once a citation is entered on a CDL holder's record as a 'plea in abeyance,' what happens to it?
choice_a: It is automatically removed after 6 months
choice_b: It only appears on the CDL MVR, not the regular MVR
choice_c: It counts as a dismissed citation with no record
choice_d: It appears on the MVR/CDL MVR and cannot be removed from the record once added
explanation: The manual states that once a plea in abeyance has been added to a CDL holder's record, it cannot be removed from the record.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.2.7 - MVR

question: It is illegal to operate a CMV if a driver's blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is:
explanation: It is illegal to operate a CMV if the driver's BAC is .04% or more, a lower threshold than the .08% standard for non-commercial driving.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.3.2 - Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: For a first offense of driving a CMV with a BAC of .04% or higher, a driver will lose their CDL for at least:
explanation: A first offense of driving a CMV with a BAC of .04% or higher results in loss of the CDL for at least one year.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.3.2 - Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: A driver who commits a felony involving controlled substances using a CMV will:
choice_a: Lose their CDL for one year
choice_b: Lose their CDL for three years
choice_c: Only receive a fine, no CDL loss
explanation: The manual states you will lose your CDL for life if you use a CMV to commit a felony involving controlled substances.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.3.2 - Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: A driver found with any detectable amount of alcohol under .04% will be put out-of-service for:
explanation: A driver with any detectable amount of alcohol under .04% will be put out-of-service for 24 hours.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.3.2 - Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: If a first-offense disqualifying violation (such as DUI) occurs while the driver is operating a CMV placarded for hazardous materials, the CDL loss is increased to at least:
explanation: The manual states you will lose your CDL for at least three years if a disqualifying first offense occurs while operating a CMV placarded for hazardous materials.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.3.2 - Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: What happens on a second offense of one of the major disqualifying violations (e.g., DUI, leaving the scene of a CMV accident)?
choice_a: The driver loses their CDL for another year
choice_b: The driver only faces a fine
choice_c: The driver loses their CDL for life
choice_d: The driver is placed on probation with no license impact
explanation: The manual states a driver will lose their CDL for life for a second offense of the listed major disqualifying violations.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.3.2 - Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: Per the Utah Driver License Division, what is the minimum age to apply for a Utah CDL, assuming the applicant already holds at least one year of Class D license experience?
explanation: According to the Utah DLD, CDL applicants must be at least 18 years old and have held a Class D license for at least one year.
source_note: dld.utah.gov/cdl-info/

question: What is the Utah CDL skills test fee for two attempts?
explanation: The Utah CDL skills (driving) test fee is $78 for two attempts, with a $52 fee for subsequent retakes.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 1.6 - Driver License Fees / dld.utah.gov/cdl-driving-test/
